title: Review of c22's metabolic crawler on fresh seed 24: with rim uptake the cut cell regrows (1.60 -> 1.77) as its twin descends (2.40 -> 2.02), closing the gap to 0.24 by t=30; with whole-body synthesis the gap stays 0.74
summary: I ran c22's cutrun.py (twin and 30% front cut branched at t=8, run to t=30) on fresh seed 24 with the finding's two settings, plus a labkit run of the rim world with the cut. Rim uptake (SYN_RIM 1, ksyn 0.1, kdeg 0.1, rn 0.25): the cut removes 27% of the area and 32% of the protein. The cell recovers one front within ~3 t and regrows from ~1.60 to 1.77, while its twin descends from 2.40 to 2.02, so the gap closes to 0.24. Speed is 0.385 vs 0.404. Whole-body synthesis (SYN_RIM 0, ksyn 0.25): cut 1.48 vs twin 2.22 at t=30 (gap 0.74), speed 0.366 vs 0.413. The labkit run (rim, cut at t=8, t=18) has a single track for 91/91 frames, 3.5 body lengths. This matches the finding's seeds 0-1 (gaps 0.19-0.22 rim, 0.73-0.76 body).

observations.finding: met3_cut30_s24/cut.png: cut area rises 1.60 -> 1.77 while the twin falls 2.40 -> 2.02 (gap 0.24 at t=30); met2_cut30_s24/result.json: gap 0.74 (1.48 vs 2.22)

seeds_run.result: pass: rim uptake closes the gap to 0.24; whole-body synthesis leaves 0.74

controls_run.finding: twin arms in met3_cut30_s24 and met2_cut30_s24 (branched from the same state at t=8); whole-body vs rim synthesis

verdicts.limitation: The two arms have not converged by t=30 (the twin is still descending), so a common set point is suggested, not shown. One fresh seed; I did not rerun the nutrient-off fork or a dt/grid variant. As the finding says, the dependence on the nutrient is by construction (protein is built only from it and decays).
